You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Financial Accounting (FI).

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: General Ledger and the Universal Journal (ACDOCA), Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Asset Accounting, Bank & Cash Management, tax handling, financial statements, period-end close.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Universal-journal ledger with hierarchical configurable chart of accounts; strict double-entry (debits == credits per currency or rejected); posted entries immutable, corrections via reversing entries only; journal lines carry cost center, profit center, project dimensions; fiscal years/periods with open/closed states enforced at service AND DB level; multi-currency (transaction + functional currency, rates table, realized/unrealized FX accounts); AP (vendor bills, payment runs, aging); AR (invoices, receipts, dunning levels, aging); configurable tax codes (rate, jurisdiction, inclusive/exclusive) at line level; statements generated from the ledger never stored (Trial Balance, P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow indirect); bank reconciliation via CSV statement import + match suggestions; asset accounting lite (asset register, straight-line and declining-balance depreciation runs posting journals).

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

Based on the web search results, here's comprehensive information about SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting FI scope, Universal Journal, ACDOCA, and its capabilities in 2025:

## Universal Journal Overview

In SAP S/4HANA Finance, the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA) is the unified foundation that merges previously distinct components of Financial Accounting (FI), Controlling (CO), Asset Accounting (AA), and others into a single data structure.

## Consolidation of Data Sources

The Universal Journal consolidates the line items from BSEG, COEP, ANEP, MLIT, and others into the ACDOCA table. This provides a single source of truth across legal and management accounting.

## Key Capabilities and Benefits

The universal journal contains the journal entries generated by FI and CO transactions and thus represents the single source of truth in SAP S/4HANA. Integrity of financial data is guaranteed by design, eliminating reconciliation effort between FI and CO and ensuring that everyone can always access the most current data.

Table ACDOCA contains all the details of the financial document and stores all fields relevant for accounting processes and reporting.

## Multidimensional Reporting

The Universal Journal provides immediate availability of multi-dimensional financial data (e.g., cost center, profit center, functional area). These fields can be exposed in CDS views and are the core of most financial reporting use cases.

## Extensibility Options

"Classic" Coding Block extensions using the OXK3 transaction and the CI_COBL structure are available. You can easily extend many processes that lead to journal entries in the ACDOCA table.

## Increased Line Item Capacity

The maximum number of posting lines in table ACDOCA is 999,999.

These capabilities demonstrate how the Universal Journal in ACDOCA forms the foundation of modern financial accounting in SAP S/4HANA, enabling real-time reporting, integrated data management, and streamlined financial processes.

# SAP S/4HANA Finance Module: Core Capabilities

Based on the webpage content, here are the primary components:

**General Ledger (GL) Accounting**
"Document splitting" enables detailed financial statements across dimensions like profit centers. The system supports "parallel accounting" for multiple accounting standards (IFRS, GAAP) and "extension ledgers" for custom fields. Real-time reporting replaces batch processing for faster insights.

**Universal Journal (ACDOCA)**
The module consolidates data from multiple tables into a single universal journal, reducing redundancy and enabling real-time financial access—a key simplification versus legacy ECC systems.

**Accounts Payable (AP) & Accounts Receivable (AR)**
Features include vendor/customer master data management, automated payment processing with payment proposals and runs, credit limit management, and "Collections and dispute management" for overdue receivables and resolutions.

**Asset Accounting (AA)**
Supports multiple depreciation methods, periodic revaluation tasks, capital work-in-progress (CWIP) management, and asset lifecycle events including transfers and retirement handling.

**Cash & Bank Management**
Provides real-time cash positioning across consolidated accounts, cash flow forecasting using predictive analytics, and standardized "Bank communication management" supporting ISO 20022 and SWIFT formats.

**Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)**
Includes budgeting, forecasting, profitability analysis across product/customer dimensions, and integration with SAP Analytics Cloud for advanced reporting.

**Period-End Close & Consolidation**
A "Closing cockpit" centralizes closing tasks, with automated intercompany reconciliation and consolidated reporting across accounting standards.

Tax codes determine calculations required for taxation functions, verify the tax type and determine the G/L account to be posted. SAP S/4HANA supports various tax systems, including sales and purchase tax, US sales tax, country-specific taxes and withholding tax.

## Electronic Bank Statement Reconciliation

The bank subaccount is linked to a bank reconciliation account in the Manage G/L Account Master Data app. The payment method is enabled for payment processing using the bank reconciliation account.

## Dunning Process

The search results indicate that dunning procedures are part of the receivables management process in S/4HANA, though specific details weren't extensively covered in these results.

## Payment Run (F110)

Transaction code F110 is used for the Automatic Payment Program (APP), facilitating the processing and printing of payments to vendors or other entities, including checks. F110 helps companies manage a high volume of payments, ensuring timely and accurate payments while minimizing manual effort and reducing errors.

Payment Proposal: It generates a list of invoices to be paid based on defined criteria (e.g., company code, payment method, vendor). Payment Run: It processes the payment proposal, creating payment documents and potentially printing checks or other payment media.

These processes work together as essential components of the SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting module.

input.overview: SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting (FI) centers on the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA), which merges general ledger, controlling, asset, and material-ledger line items into one multi-dimensional single source of truth, eliminating FI/CO reconciliation. Around that core sit Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, automatic payment runs), Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, dunning, incoming payments), Asset Accounting (ledger-based parallel valuation and depreciation), Bank and Cash Management (electronic bank statement processing, cash position), tax determination via tax codes and procedures, real-time financial statements drawn directly from the journal, and orchestrated period-end/year-end close (including the cloud Advanced Financial Closing product). Distinctive S/4HANA traits practitioners flag as essential include parallel ledgers for multi-GAAP accounting, document splitting for dimension-complete balance sheets, up to 10 parallel currencies, and posting-period control. Findings come from live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAPinsider, ERP Research, IBM, SAP Community) conducted for this task, supplemented by embedded knowledge of standard FI transactions.

capabilities.capability: General Ledger on the Universal Journal (ACDOCA)
capabilities.description: Single journal-entry table unifying FI/CO/AA line items with full dimensionality (cost center, profit center, segment, project), document principle, and immutable postings corrected by reversal.

capabilities.capability: Chart of accounts and fiscal year / posting period control
capabilities.description: Hierarchical chart of accounts plus fiscal year variants and posting period open/close control (OB52-style) that blocks postings into closed periods.

capabilities.capability: Multi-currency accounting and foreign currency valuation
capabilities.description: S/4HANA carries up to 10 parallel currencies per ledger (transaction, local, group, freely defined) with exchange-rate tables and period-end FX valuation posting realized/unrealized gains and losses.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only transaction + functional currency with rates table and realized/unrealized FX accounts; no group/additional parallel currencies or consolidation-style currency translation.
capabilities.later_path: Add extra currency amount columns per journal line plus a translation run, keeping the same rates-table and FX-account machinery.

capabilities.capability: Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, payment runs, aging)
capabilities.description: Vendor master data, invoice posting, open-item management, automatic payment program (F110-style proposal then run), and payables aging analysis.
capabilities.reason: Core AP (vendor bills, payment runs, aging) is planned; bank payment file formats (ISO 20022/NACHA) and withholding tax are not explicitly in v1.
capabilities.later_path: Layer payment-media file generation and withholding tax codes onto the existing payment-run engine.

capabilities.capability: Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, receipts, dunning, aging)
capabilities.description: Customer master data, invoice posting, incoming payment application and clearing, multi-level dunning procedures, and receivables aging.

Asset master records with depreciation areas tied to ledgers, acquisitions, multiple depreciation methods, intra/intercompany transfers, retirements with gain/loss, and assets under construction (CWIP).
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 is 'asset accounting lite': register plus straight-line and declining-balance depreciation runs posting journals; no parallel depreciation areas, transfers, retirements with gain/loss, revaluation, or assets under construction.
capabilities.later_path: Extend the asset register with lifecycle events (transfer/retire/AuC settle) and per-ledger depreciation areas reusing the existing depreciation-run poster.

capabilities.description: House bank management, electronic bank statement import (MT940/CAMT.053) with automatic matching and clearing, bank communication (SWIFT/ISO 20022), cash position and liquidity forecast.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 covers bank reconciliation via CSV statement import with match suggestions only; no standard bank formats (MT940/CAMT), no auto-clearing rules engine, no cash positioning or liquidity forecasting.
capabilities.later_path: Add MT940/CAMT.053 parsers feeding the same import pipeline, then a cash-position report over bank-clearing accounts.

capabilities.capability: Tax handling (tax codes, determination, compliance reporting)
capabilities.description: Configurable tax codes within country tax procedures, jurisdiction-based determination (US sales tax, VAT), withholding tax, external tax engine integration, and statutory tax returns/reporting.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans line-level configurable tax codes (rate, jurisdiction, inclusive/exclusive) — the calculation core — but no withholding tax, no statutory tax return reports, and no external tax engine integration.
capabilities.later_path: Build tax-return reports as queries over tax-coded journal lines and add a pluggable external tax-calculation interface.

capabilities.description: Trial balance, balance sheet, P&L, and cash flow generated in real time directly from the Universal Journal via financial statement versions and embedded analytics, with no stored aggregates.

Orchestrated close: accruals, FX valuation, GR/IR regrouping, depreciation runs, balance carryforward into the new fiscal year, and task orchestration via closing cockpit / Advanced Financial Closing.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 has the enforcement primitives (period open/close at service and DB level, FX revaluation accounts, depreciation runs) but no year-end balance carryforward, accrual engine, GR/IR regrouping, or close task orchestration.
capabilities.later_path: Add a balance-carryforward job and a simple checklist-style close task list on top of existing period states.

capabilities.description: Multiple standard and extension ledgers valuing the same transactions under different accounting principles (IFRS/local GAAP), with document splitting producing dimension-complete balance sheets per profit center/segment.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans a single universal-journal ledger; no parallel/extension ledgers or document splitting — the boundary is single-GAAP, entity-level balance sheets only (dimensions exist on lines but are not balanced).
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a ledger dimension on journal entries so postings can fan out to parallel ledgers, then add a splitting rule engine at posting time.

capabilities.capability: Credit, collections and dispute management (Receivables Management/FSCM)
capabilities.description: Credit limit checks and scoring, collections worklists, and dispute case processing layered on top of core AR in S/4HANA.
capabilities.reason: Not in the Atlas v1 plan; v1 AR stops at invoices, receipts, dunning levels, and aging — credit/collections/disputes are S/4HANA add-on processes beyond core FI-AR.
capabilities.later_path: Add credit limits on the customer master with a posting-time check, then collections worklists driven by the existing aging data.

content.text: Research complete. Structured output delivered with 12 FI capabilities judged against the Atlas v1 scope: 5 full (GL/Universal Journal, CoA and period control, AP, AR, financial statements), 5 partial (multi-currency, asset accounting, bank/cash management, tax, period-end close), and 2 out-of-scope (parallel ledgers/document splitting, credit/collections/disputes), based on live web research of SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAPinsider, ERP Research, and IBM sources.
